A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UrbanFusion/SMF study and contain readable main texts and complete appendices. Corresponding methods, equations, figures and tables can be matched despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original urban prediction experiments, cross-regional evaluations, synthetic information-preservation experiments and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds architectural controls, feature-concatenation comparisons, independent pretraining runs, city-wise results and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The proposed encoders, Transformer fusion, complementary modality masking, contrastive alignment and latent reconstruction remain unchanged. The new LSTM, depth and pooling configurations are experimental ablations; they do not replace the proposed architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same PP2-M data, urban prediction tasks, geographic coverage and synthetic experiments. The added city-wise crime results concern cities already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: Appendix D.7/Table 11 adds the 'Encoded Modalities' comparator, using concatenated modality-encoder features with linear predictors. The original GeoCLIP, SatCLIP, GAIR, GPS2Vec, CSP, PDFM and Identity comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: The existing splits, metrics, pretraining budgets and downstream tuning procedures remain unchanged. Added experiments introduce per-city scoring after joint training, controls varying coordinate concatenation and fusion architecture, and a batch-size-1 coordinate-encoding latency protocol.

E4.justification: v1's appendix analyses are retained as v2 Sections D.1–D.4. New Sections D.5–D.8 test raw-coordinate dependence, encoder architecture/depth/pooling, feature concatenation and pretraining stability. City-wise crime analysis and computational-cost analysis further extend the examination of robustness and practical behavior.

E5.justification: v1 already reports variability over five downstream MLP seeds. v2 extends uncertainty reporting to five independent UrbanFusion pretraining runs with different initializations and data orderings (Table 12). Table 15 also reports timing variability over 5,000 forward passes.

E6.justification: Original benchmark values are retained, but substantial new city-wise, ablation, pretraining-variability and runtime results appear. Table 11 reports concatenation versus UrbanFusion scores of 67.3 versus 65.6 for land-cover F1 and 62.6 versus 88.5 for crime R2. Table 15 newly reports UrbanFusion inference at 6.57 ms and training at 519.30 minutes.

T1.justification: The proxy-modality assumption, Lemma 1, PID definitions and InfoNCE/Barber–Agakov derivations are retained from v1 Appendix D in v2 Appendix E. Notational corrections and citation updates do not change the mathematical argument.

C1.justification: The conclusion narrows the claim from state-of-the-art performance on 41 tasks to performance on a majority of tasks, acknowledging exceptions. Headline framing changes from a Geo-Foundation Model to a spatial/location embedding model, while the central SMF, modality-flexibility and generalization contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds task-dependent interpretations of fusion, suggesting that land-cover and coarse land-use tasks may not require fused representations. It discusses architectural robustness and training/inference cost tradeoffs, and makes applicability limits more specific to point- or postal-code-level urban data.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the satellite crop's 2240-by-2240-meter footprint, documents the additional architectural configurations, and provides detailed runtime measurements and their inference protocol. Existing implementation recipes and code, dataset and weight access information are retained; the reproducibility statement moves to Appendix B.

R1.justification: Related work expands to discuss UrbanCLIP, ReFound, GeoLink, urban region pretraining/prompting and FlexiReg, distinguishing their region-level approaches from UrbanFusion's location-level fusion. Supporting architecture citations are also added. Publication and author-name updates to existing references do not introduce new evaluated baselines.

P1.justification: The overall narrative remains recognizable, with targeted rewrites of the introduction, synthetic-experiment explanation and conclusion. Existing appendix details are explained more fully in Section 4.5, the reproducibility statement is relocated, the appendix contents page is removed, and disclosure/impact statements are added.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column conference main text, extensively resizing and repositioning figures and tables. Figure 3's panels change from side-by-side to stacked. Six new tables present additional analyses, while existing figure content and matched benchmark tables are retained.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked a direct concatenated-feature control and pretraining-level stability evidence. v2 supplies both (Tables 11–12), alongside coordinate and architecture controls, substantially strengthening validation of the central fusion contribution. It also acknowledges tasks where fusion loses and documents its higher training cost. These additions improve the evidential basis and qualification of the conclusions without replacing the original benchmark evidence.
